items.title: `HashMap` on ONE table: the two-parameter `NativeMap<K, V>` (the key beside its `Option<V>` slot, `None` a tombstone on both backends) in place of B689's two hash-keyed tables, and on it `slot(key): &mut Option<V> borrows self` + `Option::get_or_insert(&mut self, lazy v): &mut V borrows self` - the entry idiom with no handle type (`groups.slot(key).get_or_insert([]).push(row)`); `update` goes
items.kind: feature (std hash_map + vilan-rt + the JS map; M)
items.status: OPEN - RULED 2026-11-03 by the owner (owner questions 9 + 11: rec accepted); Order 56 std lane, a short paper slice first (hash-map-lend.md §9)
items.discussion: the owner 2026-11-03: the two-table layout's only benefit was delivery time (no invariant, no new runtime type inside a bug lane); its price is a second index per map, two hashes + two inserts per write, and the closure-only API - `modify` exists because the keys table needs an after-step, which is exactly what blocks a returned place. hash-map-lend.md §2 names the two-parameter NativeMap as the end state and lists its churn: a second runtime map type, HashSet on a different shape, the I1-era two-parameter bound gap to re-check, the const-map lowering to rework
items.body: The slice: (1) `NativeMap<K, V>` in vilan-rt (the entries `Vec<(K, Option<V>)>` the paper already moved the tombstone onto) and in the JS map (the stored value an `Option` object so a view is the object itself; `None` a tombstone the iteration and `contains_key` skip; `compact` as native); `HashMap` and `HashSet` over it; the bound gap and the const-map lowering re-checked; `eq`/`entries`/`keys` as today. (2) `slot(&mut self, key): &mut Option<V> borrows self` (the `Shared::write` shape: a second-class view, chainable in one expression, never stored) and `Option::get_or_insert(&mut self, lazy v): &mut V borrows self`; `update` REMOVED (no estate yet: kolt's grouping sites are still the take-copy form), `peek` kept as the read form, `modify` kept or folded into `slot` as the paper slice decides. Pins: the M182 grouping pin on the new spelling (O(1) per push), B689's lend pins unchanged, the tombstone rules on both backends by the differential (iteration order, contains_key, len, compact), the view's second-class rule refused when stored. Perf: the per-write cost measured on kolt's map-heavy sites before/after. Docs: std/collections.md's map section; CHANGELOG `breaking` (update removed). Sizing M.
